clues: This is a small city in Quebec, in eastern Canada. It stands on the banks of a river.
This place has a strange winter secret. One stretch of its river never freezes, even in winter.
In 1815, Joseph Bouchette wrote a report on this area. His report used an older name for the place.
In winter, a thaw can open the ice here. No one could see a clear reason for that thaw.
Face the river in the coldest weeks. The water right before the town stays clear of ice.
